en: Mayon Volcano has steep, perfect cone slopes because its highly viscous lava cools quickly and piles up near the vent instead of flowing far.
The southwest monsoon brings heavy rain to western Luzon because its winds pick up massive moisture from the South China Sea before hitting the mountains.
The MakBan geothermal plant in Laguna generates electricity because underground magma heats groundwater into steam, which then spins turbines to produce power.
The Puerto Princesa Underground River formed because slightly acidic rainwater slowly dissolved the surrounding limestone rock over millions of years.
The Banaue Rice Terraces prevent severe soil erosion because their carved stone walls hold water and trap soil on the steep Cordillera slopes.
Mangrove forests in Eastern Samar protect coastal towns from storm surges because their dense, tangled root systems absorb wave energy and trap sediment.
Typhoons gain immense strength over the Pacific Ocean because warm surface water evaporates rapidly, releasing latent heat that fuels the storm's powerful winds.
The Pasig River suffers from low oxygen levels because excessive organic waste from cities consumes oxygen during bacterial decomposition, suffocating aquatic life.
Taal Volcano produces violent steam explosions when rising hot magma contacts the main crater lake's water, instantly vaporizing it to blast rock fragments.
Corals in the Tubbataha Reefs build massive structures because tiny coral polyps continuously secrete calcium carbonate skeletons that accumulate over thousands of years.
Mount Apo's mossy forests capture heavy cloud moisture because their dense canopy of epiphytes and leaves intercepts fog, which then drips into the soil.
The Cagayan River forms a large delta at its mouth because the slowing water current drops its heavy sediment load into the Babuyan Channel.
